proposal.hypothesis: A two-group scalar schedule that interleaves independent table lookups may overlap lookup latency while amortizing loop control. Committing the first block only after its own validity check preserves fallback position if the second block is invalid. Prior unroll factors were slower than baseline, so this tests a scheduling variant, not an assumed speedup.

retained: Unrolled the safe decode loop by two eight-character blocks when at least 21 input characters remain.
Interleaved scalar table lookups for independent blocks, then validated and stored the first block before committing the second.
If the first block is invalid, fall through to the existing scalar decoder without advancing; if only the second is invalid, keep the first block's output and resume at the second block.
Preserved the existing scalar tail, padding, and invalid-input path; added no explicit SIMD, parallel execution, benchmark-size specialization, or thread-budget changes.

proposal.hypothesis: Prior measured 2-, 3-, 4-, and 8-group scalar unrolls were all slower than the 55.00 µs baseline. This two-group contrast keeps interleaved scalar lookups but uses byte-wise input access and exact six-byte output writes, testing whether avoiding word shuffles and overstores offsets their extra scalar instructions. No speedup is assumed; the reserved tail and unchanged scalar decoder preserve padding and fallback handling.

retained: Unrolled two independent eight-character groups and interleaved scalar byte-indexed decode-table lookups.
Validated and wrote the first group's six decoded bytes before committing the second group; invalid groups fall back to the existing scalar path.
Wrote exactly six output bytes per group and retained the 21-byte guard to leave tail and padding processing to the original decoder.
Kept encoding, threads budget, and all non-source files unchanged; added no explicit SIMD or parallel execution.

proposal.hypothesis: Prior scalar unroll choices were all slower than the 55.00 µs baseline, and the staged two-group variant failed correctness on Lena. This contrasting two-group schedule tests whether interleaved lookups followed by one combined validity branch and an all-or-nothing exact-size output commit can reduce valid-path control overhead while keeping invalid input and padding in the existing scalar path. No speedup or correctness result is assumed before controller evaluation.

retained: Changed only the bulk decode loop in src/candidate.cpp to interleave scalar table lookups for two independent eight-character groups.
Combined validity checks for both groups before storing output or advancing input, leaving an invalid group for the original scalar fallback.
Kept the existing 21-character guard, exact six-byte-per-group writes, scalar tail and padding handling, and threads behavior; added no explicit SIMD or parallel execution.
